title: Finite-momentum coupling of Higgs and Bardasis--Schrieffer modes in superconductors with competing pairing channels
authors: Samuel Awelewa, Yafis Barlas, Maxim Dzero
abstract: In superconductors with competing pairing channels, two well defined excitations exist below the pair-breaking edge: the Higgs mode of the condensed $s$-wave channel and the Bardasis--Schrieffer (BS) exciton of the subdominant $d$-wave channel. Their mixing is doubly forbidden --- by point-group symmetry at zero momentum and because the two reside in the amplitude and phase sectors of the order parameter respectively, by particle--hole symmetry at every momentum. Working in a Nambu--Keldysh quasiclassical framework extended to leading $1/\varepsilon_F$ corrections and including the self-consistently screened Coulomb potential, we show that finite momentum combined with particle--hole asymmetry generates a direct coupling which we obtain in closed form. Whether this coupling produces an avoided crossing is decided, however, not by its magnitude but by kinematics. In the clean limit the Higgs is not a sub-gap pole but a resonance pinned to the pair-breaking edge, which disperses with coefficient unity in $(v_Fq)^2$, while the bound BS mode disperses more slowly: the two branches therefore separate rather than converge and never become degenerate. The obstruction is specific to the clean limit: exact dirty-limit results show that disorder detaches the amplitude resonance from the edge and reverses its dispersion, which can result in an avoided crossing with the BS mode at intermediate scattering. In that regime, the coupling computed here would set the splitting between the hybridized branches. We discuss the experimental implications of these results.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the coupling between the Higgs mode and the Bardasis–Schrieffer exciton in superconductors with competing pairing symmetries. Using a quasiclassical approach, it finds that while symmetry forbids mixing at zero momentum, finite momentum allows coupling. Crucially, the ability to observe a resonance crossing depends critically on whether the system is clean or disordered.
main_problem: The study investigates the finite-momentum coupling between two distinct collective excitations—the Higgs mode (from $s$-wave pairing) and the Bardasis–Schrieffer (BS) exciton (from $d$-wave pairing)—in superconductors with competing pairing channels.
main_result: In the clean limit, kinematic differences cause the Higgs and BS branches to separate rather than cross. However, in the dirty limit, disorder can detach the resonance from the edge, potentially allowing for an avoided crossing set by the coupling strength $\Pi_{sd}(q, \Omega)$.
method: The analysis employs a Nambu–Keldysh quasiclassical framework extended to leading $1/\epsilon_F$ corrections and incorporates self-consistently screened Coulomb potential effects.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a superconductor exhibiting competing pairing channels ($s$-wave and $d$-wave). The theoretical machinery involves analyzing coupled order-parameter fluctuations within the quasiclassical framework.
key_observables: Higgs mode dispersion, BS exciton dispersion, the coupling function $\Pi_{sd}(q, \Omega)$, and spectral weight distribution in amplitude/phase channels.
important_parameters: Momentum ($q$), frequency ($\Omega$), clean limit vs. dirty limit (disorder strength), and the ratio of pairing gaps to Fermi energy ($\Delta/\epsilon_F$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes sharply between the clean limit (where kinematics forbid crossing) and the dirty limit (where disorder modifies dispersion relations).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the separation of branches in the clean limit due to differing momentum dispersions ($\alpha_{SH}=1$ vs. $\alpha_{BS} < 1$). Figure 2 schematically shows how moderate disorder can induce an avoided crossing.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical context and symmetry constraints (zero momentum). It then develops the theoretical framework using quasiclassical methods to calculate the coupling term in closed form. Finally, it analyzes the resulting dispersion relations by comparing the clean limit results against those modified by disorder effects.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant because it tackles collective excitations and symmetry breaking in unconventional superconductors, which are central topics in strongly correlated electron physics, often requiring advanced many-body techniques similar to those used in AMO or quantum optics for complex interacting systems.
